title: A parameterized linear formulation of the integer hull
problem:
Let \(P(b):=\{x\in \mathbb{R}^n:Ax\le b\}\). For a rational polyhedron \(Q\), let \(Q'\) denote the intersection of all Chv\u00e1tal-Gomory cuts of \(Q\), and define \(P(b)^{(0)}=P(b)\), \(P(b)^{(j+1)}=(P(b)^{(j)})'\).

Fix positive integers \(D\) and \(\Delta\). Assume that whenever
\[
Q=\{x\in \mathbb{R}^n:Mx\le d\}
\]
with \(M\in \mathbb{Z}^{t\times n}\), \(d\in \mathbb{Z}^t\), and \(\|M\|_\infty\le n^i\Delta\), its elementary closure is given by
\[
Q'=\bigcap_{\substack{\mu\in\{0,\dots,D\}^t\\ \mu^TM\equiv 0\ (\mathrm{mod}\ D)\\ |\operatorname{supp}(\mu)|\le n}}
\left\{x\in \mathbb{R}^n:\left(\frac{\mu}{D}\right)^TMx\le \left\lfloor\left(\frac{\mu}{D}\right)^Td\right\rfloor\right\}.
\]

Suppose that for some \(i\ge 0\) and \(r\in \mathbb{Z}^m\) there exist an integer \(m'\ge 1\), a matrix \(B\in \mathbb{Z}^{m'\times n}\), a matrix \(C\in \mathbb{Z}^{m'\times m}\), and a vector \(f_r\in \mathbb{Z}^{m'}\) such that
\[
\|B\|_\infty\le n^i\Delta
\]
and
\[
P(b)^{(i)}=\left\{x\in \mathbb{R}^n:Bx\le f_r+\frac{C(b-r)}{D^i}\right\}
\]
for every \(b\in \mathbb{Z}^m\) satisfying \(b-r\in D^i\mathbb{Z}^m\).

Prove that there exist integer matrices \(B'\), \(C'\), and an integer vector \(f_r'\), depending only on \(r,B,C,f_r\), such that for every \(b\in \mathbb{Z}^m\) with \(b-r\in D^{i+1}\mathbb{Z}^m\),
\[
P(b)^{(i+1)}=\left\{x\in \mathbb{R}^n:B'x\le f_r'+\frac{C'(b-r)}{D^{i+1}}\right\},
\]
and
\[
\|B'\|_\infty\le n^{i+1}\Delta.
\]

\Bigl\lfloor \Bigl(\frac{\mu}{D}\Bigr)^T (f_r + D\,Ck) \Bigr\rfloor = q + \mu^T Ck .

\mu^T B\,x \le Dq + D\,\mu^T Ck .

Expanding gives \(\mu^T f_r/D + \mu^T C y\); the floor separates additively because \(\mu^T C y\) is integer, yielding \(\lfloor\mu^T f_r/D\rfloor + \mu^T C y = c_\mu + d_\mu y\). Multiplying through by \(D\) and using \(D\mid\mu^T B\) produces \(a_\mu x \le c_\mu + d_\mu y\).

Collecting all such inequalities, the representation follows. The step also constructs the matrices and vector:  
\[
B' = \begin{pmatrix} a_{\mu_1} \\ \vdots \\ a_{\mu_N} \end{pmatrix},\quad
C' = \begin{pmatrix} d_{\mu_1} \\ \vdots \\ d_{\mu_N} \end{pmatrix},\quad
f_r' = \begin{pmatrix} c_{\mu_1} \\ \vdots \\ c_{\mu_N} \end{pmatrix},
\]  
so that  
\[
P(b)^{(i+1)} = \bigl\{x : B'x \le f_r' + C'(b-r)/D^{i+1}\bigr\}.
\]

The norm bound \(\|B'\|_\infty\le n^{i+1}\Delta\) is verified entry‑wise: for any admissible \(\mu\) and any column \(\ell\),  
\[
|(a_\mu)_\ell| = \frac{1}{D}\Bigl|\sum_{j\in\operatorname{supp}(\mu)} \mu_j B_{j\ell}\Bigr| \le \frac{n\cdot D\cdot \|B\|_\infty}{D} = n\cdot n^i\Delta = n^{i+1}\Delta.
\]  
All constructed objects depend only on \(r,B,C,f_r\) and the fixed parameters \(D,n,m'\); no extra congruence data about \(b\) are required.

The step concludes by stating that the lemma is fully resolved; the inductive step is now formalised and the uniform dependence on \(b\) is fully explicit.

final_answer:
We are given positive integers \(D,\Delta\) and an integer \(i\ge0\).  Fix a residue vector \(r\in\mathbb{Z}^m\) and assume that there exist an integer \(m'\ge 1\), matrices \(B\in\mathbb{Z}^{m'\times n},\,C\in\mathbb{Z}^{m'\times m}\), and a vector \(f_r\in\mathbb{Z}^{m'}\) with \(\|B\|_\infty\le n^i\Delta\) such that for every \(b\in\mathbb{Z}^m\) satisfying \(b-r\in D^i\mathbb{Z}^m\),

\[
P(b)^{(i)} = \Bigl\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n : Bx \le f_r + \frac{C(b-r)}{D^i}\Bigr\}.
\tag{1}
\]

We must prove that there exist integer matrices \(B',C'\) and an integer vector \(f_r'\), depending only on \(r,B,C,f_r\), such that for every \(b\in\mathbb{Z}^m\) with \(b-r\in D^{i+1}\mathbb{Z}^m\),

\[
P(b)^{(i+1)} = \Bigl\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n : B'x \le f_r' + \frac{C'(b-r)}{D^{i+1}}\Bigr\},
\tag{2}
\]

and \(\|B'\|_\infty\le n^{i+1}\Delta\).

---

### Proof

Let \(b\in\mathbb{Z}^m\) be any vector such that \(b-r\in D^{i+1}\mathbb{Z}^m\).  Write  

\[
b = r + D^{i+1}y,\qquad y\in\mathbb{Z}^m.
\]

Because \(b-r = D^{i+1}y \in D^i\mathbb{Z}^m\), condition (1) applies to this \(b\).  Substituting,

\[
P(b)^{(i)} = \Bigl\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n : Bx \le f_r + D\,C y\Bigr\}.
\tag{3}
\]

The right‑hand side is an integer vector because \(f_r\) and \(D\,C y\) are integer.  The polyhedron in (3) is therefore an integer polyhedron whose defining matrix \(B\) satisfies \(\|B\|_\infty\le n^i\Delta\).  The problem statement assumes that for every polyhedron of the form \(\{x: Mx\le d\}\) with integer \(M,d\) and \(\|M\|_\infty\le n^i\Delta\), its elementary closure is given by

\[
\{x: Mx\le d\}' = \bigcap_{\substack{\mu\in\{0,\dots,D\}^{t}\\ \mu^{\mathsf T}M\equiv0\;(\mathrm{mod}\;D)\\ |\operatorname{supp}(\mu)|\le n}}
\Bigl\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n : \Bigl(\frac{\mu}{D}\Bigr)^{\mathsf T}Mx \le \Bigl\lfloor\Bigl(\frac{\mu}{D}\Bigr)^{\mathsf T}d\Bigr\rfloor\Bigr\}.
\tag{4}
\]

(Here \(t\) is the number of rows of \(M\); in our case \(t=m'\) and the condition applies to \(M=B,\; d=f_r+D\,C y\).)  
Applying (4) to the polyhedron in (3) we obtain, for this particular \(b\),

\[
P(b)^{(i+1)} = \bigcap_{\mathcal{M}}\;
\Bigl\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n : \Bigl(\frac{\mu}{D}\Bigr)^{\mathsf T}B\,x \le
\Bigl\lfloor\Bigl(\frac{\mu}{D}\Bigr)^{\mathsf T}(f_r+D\,C y)\Bigr\rfloor\Bigr\},
\tag{5}
\]

where \(\mathcal{M}\) denotes the finite set of all \(\mu\in\{0,\dots,D\}^{m'}\) satisfying  

\[
\mu^{\mathsf T}B\equiv0\pmod D,\qquad |\operatorname{supp}(\mu)|\le n.
\]

The set \(\mathcal{M}\) depends only on the fixed data \(B,D,n,m'\); it is the same for every \(b\) in our considered progression.  For a fixed \(\mu\in\mathcal{M}\) we expand the right‑hand side:

\[
\Bigl(\frac{\mu}{D}\Bigr)^{\mathsf T}(f_r+D\,C y) = \frac{\mu^{\mathsf T}f_r}{D} + \mu^{\mathsf T}C y .
\]

Because \(y\) is an integer vector and \(C\) is an integer matrix, \(\mu^{\mathsf T}C y\) is an integer.  Write \(\mu^{\mathsf T}f_r = Dq + s\) with \(0\le s<D\); then

\[
\Bigl\lfloor\frac{\mu^{\mathsf T}f_r}{D} + \mu^{\mathsf T}C y\Bigr\rfloor
= q + \mu^{\mathsf T}C y
= \Bigl\lfloor\frac{\mu^{\mathsf T}f_r}{D}\Bigr\rfloor + \mu^{\mathsf T}C y .
\]

Thus each inequality in (5) becomes

\[
\frac{\mu^{\mathsf T}B}{D}\,x \le \Bigl\lfloor\frac{\mu^{\mathsf T}f_r}{D}\Bigr\rfloor + \mu^{\mathsf T}C y .
\tag{6}
\]

Since \(\mu^{\mathsf T}B\) is divisible by \(D\), the vector \(\frac{\mu^{\mathsf T}B}{D}\) has integer entries.  Substituting back \(y = (b-r)/D^{i+1}\) gives

\[
\frac{\mu^{\mathsf T}B}{D}\,x \le \Bigl\lfloor\frac{\mu^{\mathsf T}f_r}{D}\Bigr\rfloor + \frac{\mu^{\mathsf T}C\,(b-r)}{D^{i+1}}.
\tag{7}
\]

Intersecting over all \(\mu\in\mathcal{M}\) yields

\[
P(b)^{(i+1)} = \bigcap_{\mu\in\mathcal{M}}
\Bigl\{ x\in\mathbb{R}^n : \frac{\mu^{\mathsf T}B}{D}\,x \le \Bigl\lfloor\frac{\mu^{\mathsf T}f_r}{D}\Bigr\rfloor + \frac{\mu^{\mathsf T}C\,(b-r)}{D^{i+1}} \Bigr\}.
\tag{8}
\]

Now define the integer matrices and vector as follows.  For each \(\mu\in\mathcal{M}\) set

\[
B'_\mu = \frac{\mu^{\mathsf T}B}{D},\qquad
C'_\mu = \mu^{\mathsf T}C,\qquad
f_r'(\mu) = \Bigl\lfloor\frac{\mu^{\mathsf T}f_r}{D}\Bigr\rfloor .
\]

Arrange the rows of these objects in any order to form matrices \(B'\in\mathbb{Z}^{M\times n}\), \(C'\in\mathbb{Z}^{M\times m}\) and a vector \(f_r'\in\mathbb{Z}^{M}\), where \(M=|\mathcal{M}|\).  Then (8) is exactly the system

\[
B'x \le f_r' + \frac{C'(b-r)}{D^{i+1}}.
\]

Hence for every \(b\) with \(b-r\in D^{i+1}\mathbb{Z}^m\),

\[
P(b)^{(i+1)} = \Bigl\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n : B'x \le f_r' + \frac{C'(b-r)}{D^{i+1}}\Bigr\}.
\]

It remains to verify the norm bound on \(B'\).  Take any \(\mu\in\mathcal{M}\) and any column index \(\ell\in\{1,\dots,n\}\).  Because \(|\mu_j|\le D\) for all \(j\) and \(|\operatorname{supp}(\mu)|\le n\),

\[
\Bigl|\bigl(\frac{\mu^{\mathsf T}B}{D}\bigr)_\ell\Bigr|
= \frac{1}{D}\Bigl|\sum_{j\in\operatorname{supp}(\mu)} \mu_j\,B_{j\ell}\Bigr|
\le \frac{1}{D}\sum_{j\in\operatorname{supp}(\mu)} |\mu_j|\,|B_{j\ell}|
\le \frac{1}{D}\cdot n\cdot D\cdot\|B\|_\infty
= n\,\|B\|_\infty .
\]

By the induction hypothesis (the given condition for index \(i\)) we have \(\|B\|_\infty\le n^i\Delta\).  Consequently

\[
\Bigl|\bigl(B'\bigr)_{\mu,\ell}\Bigr| \le n\cdot n^i\Delta = n^{i+1}\Delta .
\]

Since this bound is independent of the particular \(\mu\) and \(\ell\), we obtain \(\|B'\|_\infty\le n^{i+1}\Delta\).  All constructed objects \(B',C',f_r'\) depend only on the fixed data \(r,B,C,f_r\) (and the parameters \(D,n,m'\)), as required.

Thus the statement is proved. ∎

reference_answer:
Fix \(b\in \mathbb{Z}^m\) with \(b-r\in D^{i+1}\mathbb{Z}^m\). Then in particular \(b-r\in D^i\mathbb{Z}^m\), so the assumed description of \(P(b)^{(i)}\) applies. Set
\[
d_b:=f_r+\frac{C(b-r)}{D^i}.
\]
Because \(C\) is integral and each entry of \(b-r\) is divisible by \(D^i\), we have \(d_b\in \mathbb{Z}^{m'}\). Hence
\[
P(b)^{(i)}=\{x\in \mathbb{R}^n:Bx\le d_b\}.
\]

Since \(\|B\|_\infty\le n^i\Delta\), we may apply the assumed one-step description with \(M=B\) and \(d=d_b\). Writing
\[
T:=T(B)=\left\{\mu\in \{0,\dots,D\}^{m'} : \mu^T B\equiv 0 \pmod D,\ |\operatorname{supp}(\mu)|\le n\right\},
\]
we obtain
\[
P(b)^{(i+1)}=(P(b)^{(i)})'=
\bigcap_{\mu\in T}
\left\{x\in \mathbb{R}^n:
\left(\frac{\mu}{D}\right)^T Bx
\le
\left\lfloor \left(\frac{\mu}{D}\right)^T d_b\right\rfloor
\right\}.
\]
So it remains to rewrite the right-hand side of each such inequality in the desired affine form.

Take any \(\mu\in T\). Using the definition of \(d_b\),
\[
\left\lfloor \left(\frac{\mu}{D}\right)^T d_b\right\rfloor
=
\left\lfloor \left(\frac{\mu}{D}\right)^T\! f_r
+ \left(\frac{\mu}{D}\right)^T \frac{C(b-r)}{D^i}\right\rfloor
=
\left\lfloor \left(\frac{\mu}{D}\right)^T\! f_r
+ \frac{\mu^T C(b-r)}{D^{i+1}}\right\rfloor.
\]
Now \(\mu^T C\) is an integer row vector, and every coordinate of \(b-r\) is divisible by \(D^{i+1}\). Therefore
\[
\frac{\mu^T C(b-r)}{D^{i+1}}\in \mathbb{Z}.
\]
Call this integer \(z_{\mu,b}\). Then
\[
\left\lfloor \left(\frac{\mu}{D}\right)^T\! f_r + z_{\mu,b}\right\rfloor
=
\left\lfloor \left(\frac{\mu}{D}\right)^T\! f_r\right\rfloor + z_{\mu,b}
=
\left\lfloor \left(\frac{\mu}{D}\right)^T\! f_r\right\rfloor
+
\frac{\mu^T C(b-r)}{D^{i+1}}.
\]
Thus each defining cut of \(P(b)^{(i+1)}\) can be written as
\[
\left(\frac{\mu}{D}\right)^T Bx
\le
\left\lfloor \left(\frac{\mu}{D}\right)^T\! f_r\right\rfloor
+
\frac{\mu^T C(b-r)}{D^{i+1}}.
\]

This suggests the following choices, with rows indexed by \(\mu\in T\):
\[
B' := \left(\left(\frac{\mu}{D}\right)^T B\right)_{\mu\in T},
\qquad
f_r' := \left(\left\lfloor \left(\frac{\mu}{D}\right)^T f_r\right\rfloor\right)_{\mu\in T},
\qquad
C' := (\mu^T C)_{\mu\in T}.
\]
These objects depend only on \(r,B,C,f_r\) (indeed, \(T\) depends only on \(B\)) and not on the chosen \(b\).

We now verify integrality.

1. \(f_r'\in \mathbb{Z}^{|T|}\) is immediate from the floor.

2. \(C'\in \mathbb{Z}^{|T|\times m}\) because both \(\mu\) and \(C\) are integral.

3. For \(B'\), since \(\mu\in T\) satisfies \(\mu^T B\equiv 0 \pmod D\), every entry of the integer row vector \(\mu^T B\) is divisible by \(D\). Hence \(((\mu/D)^T B)\) is an integer row vector. Therefore \(B'\in \mathbb{Z}^{|T|\times n}\).

With these definitions, the previous calculation shows that for every \(b\) with \(b-r\in D^{i+1}\mathbb{Z}^m\),
\[
P(b)^{(i+1)}=
\left\{x\in \mathbb{R}^n:
B'x\le f_r' + \frac{C'(b-r)}{D^{i+1}}
\right\}.
\]
This is exactly the required form.

It remains to prove the norm bound on \(B'\). Fix a row of \(B'\) corresponding to some \(\mu\in T\), and fix a column index \(j\in\{1,\dots,n\}\). Then
\[
\left|\left(\left(\frac{\mu}{D}\right)^T B\right)_j\right|
=
\left|\sum_{\ell=1}^{m'} \frac{\mu_\ell}{D} B_{\ell j}\right|
\le
\sum_{\ell\in \operatorname{supp}(\mu)} \frac{\mu_\ell}{D}\, |B_{\ell j}|.
\]
Because \(0\le \mu_\ell\le D\), we have \(\mu_\ell/D\le 1\). Also \(|\operatorname{supp}(\mu)|\le n\) and \(|B_{\ell j}|\le \|B\|_\infty\). Hence
\[
\left|\left(\left(\frac{\mu}{D}\right)^T B\right)_j\right|
\le
|\operatorname{supp}(\mu)|\,\|B\|_\infty
\le n\,\|B\|_\infty
\le n\cdot n^i\Delta
= n^{i+1}\Delta.
\]
Taking the maximum over all rows and columns gives
\[
\|B'\|_\infty\le n^{i+1}\Delta.
\]

Therefore the next elementary closure again has an affine right-hand side on the residue class \(r \bmod D^{i+1}\), with the claimed norm bound. This proves the statement.
